title: The Colosseum
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck (with iHeart Intro voice) discuss the Colosseum in ancient Rome: its origins under Vespasian and Titus on the site of Nero's Golden House, the name derived from a colossal statue of Nero, its construction and engineering (concrete, foundations, awning, hypogeum), the seating hierarchy and tickets, the animal hunts, public executions, gladiator types and training, notable gladiators like Flamma, Commodus, the Christian martyrdom association, and the building's decline, earthquakes, medieval reuse, and restoration. Ends with a listener mail story about a skydiving tooth loss.

segments.title: Opening banter and Rome travel
segments.summary: Hosts chat about visiting Rome and the Colosseum, and about how attractive Italians are.

segments.title: Stadium crowd and the Colosseum's reputation
segments.summary: Discussion of the claimed fifteen-minute evacuation of a crowd of about 87,000, a joke about stadium parking, and an overview of the Colosseum as a feat of engineering that survived earthquakes.

segments.title: Origins of amphitheaters and the Senate ban
segments.summary: Explains that amphitheaters were first fully encircled theaters, that the Roman Senate banned permanent theaters, and mentions Pliny's account of a temporary wooden theater.

segments.title: Vespasian, Nero and the name Colosseum
segments.summary: Covers Nero's reign, the Great Fire of 64, the Flavian dynasty under Vespasian, funding from the Jerusalem war spoils, building on the site of Nero's Golden House, and the name from a colossal statue of Nero.

segments.title: Building dimensions and foundations
segments.summary: Gives the building's size and materials, and explains that its deep concrete foundation on wetlands helped it survive earthquakes. Discusses Roman concrete and quicklime.

segments.title: Architecture, awning and arena floor
segments.summary: Describes the column orders from Doric to Corinthian, the retractable awning, the arena floor size, the sand covering, and the eight-year construction and dedication under Titus.

segments.title: Hypogeum and underground machinery
segments.summary: Describes the underground hypogeum built under Domitian, with trap doors, pulleys and elevators used to bring animals and gladiators up into the arena.

segments.title: Seating, social hierarchy and the podium barrier
segments.summary: Covers the protective stone barrier and bronze fence, the seating for senators and emperor, the equestrian class, and the subdivided seating by social group and standing room cheap seats.

segments.title: Banned professions and Colosseum tickets
segments.summary: Discusses groups banned from attending (gravediggers, actors, former gladiators) and the pottery shard tickets with gate and seat information, plus free admission and plumbing.

segments.title: Opening games and animal hunts
segments.summary: Describes the 100 days of games at the opening, the procession, the imported exotic animals, the venatores hunts, animal-versus-animal fights, and cleanup of carcasses.

segments.title: Noon executions and Christian martyrs
segments.summary: Covers the midday public executions, mythological reenactments, and the persecution of Christians including Ignatius of Antioch, with the hosts' tangent about a bartender's football joke.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break; comedy tangent about a Nate Bargatze special before the break.

segments.title: Gladiator types, training and fame
segments.summary: Explains gladiator categories (Murmillo, Thraxian, Retiarius, Essedarius, Hoplomachus), the rarity of fights to the death because of training costs, how events were funded and organized, and Flamma the Syrian gladiator who refused freedom.
topics: gladiator fights to the death misconception

segments.title: Commodus and naumachia mock naval battles
segments.summary: Describes the emperor Commodus fighting in the arena and his cruelty, the financing of events, and the debate over whether the Colosseum or a separate Tiber-side basin hosted mock naval battles.

segments.title: Decline, medieval reuse, restoration and tourism
segments.summary: Covers the decline of gladiatorial games with the rise of Christianity, earthquakes in 443 and 1349, medieval reuse and stone scavenging, Pope Benedict XIV's 1749 blessing, unification-era protection, Mussolini-era excavation, modern restoration and six million annual visitors.

segments.title: Listener mail: skydiving tooth
segments.summary: Listener Aaron Bogan describes losing a front flipper tooth during a skydive for her husband's birthday; the hosts read the email and promote sending in stories.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Standard closing credits for Stuff You Should Know.
